name: @test-cabinet/structured-3d
description: The Structured 3D engine: the runtime a produced 3D game is built inside. An engine is created over a canvas and bound to one game definition, and it owns the gameplay framework the game subclasses — worlds built from level descriptions, the game mode and game state that decide a match, actors assembled from components, and the controllers that possess and drive pawns — together with the frame loop and its replaceable clock, engine-owned WebGL2 rendering with its layer-ordered pipeline and render modes, collision detection with volumetric shapes reported as events and manifolds, the letterboxed device-pixel-ratio-aware canvas fit and the frustum camera that projects world units into it, named input actions read only through a player controller, an audio cue bus with its first-gesture unlock, asset loading for meshes, textures, materials, and audio under a fixed root, a diagnostics overlay, the debug surface a game instance returns from its initialize, and an opt-in draw-command recorder whose recordings replay the frames a build drew — leaving the game to write only its own rules and behavior. Everything it does is observed by subscribing to its events rather than by reading a log it accumulates.
